cards.explanation: The answer is: so they do not profane His holy name. God says to treat the sacred offerings with respect "…so that they do not profane My holy name." (Leviticus 22:2) These offerings were consecrated to Him, so how the priests handled them mattered. Treat them casually and you're treating His name casually.

The answer is: he must be cut off from God's presence. God says that person "…must be cut off from My presence." (Leviticus 22:3) This is for the generations to come, friends, so it isn't just a one-time rule for that week. Coming near the sacred offerings while unclean is serious business.

The answer is True. God says the priests must keep His charge, "…lest they bear the guilt and die because they profane it." (Leviticus 22:9) It's a heavy warning, and I'll say it plainly: this one is serious. Then He adds that He is the One who sanctifies them.

The answer is the LORD Himself. God says, "I am the LORD who sanctifies them." (Leviticus 22:9) The priests keep the charge, but the holy-making is His work. I like that, friends, because I couldn't make myself holy any more than a worn-out cookie stamper could make himself shiny again.

The answer is the punishment for guilt. If the priests let the people eat the sacred offerings, the people would "…bear the punishment for guilt." (Leviticus 22:16) So the priests' care protects the people too. God closes that thought with the words, "I am the LORD who sanctifies them."

The answer is male. The offering must be "…an unblemished male from the cattle, sheep, or goats in order for it to be accepted on your behalf." (Leviticus 22:19) Both parts count, friends: male and unblemished. God is specific, and I respect a recipe that's specific.

The answer is False. The text says a peace offering "…must be without blemish or defect to be acceptable." (Leviticus 22:21) A small blemish doesn't get a pass, friends. It's the same standard God gave for the burnt offering.

The answer is a foreigner. God says, "Neither you nor a foreigner shall present food to your God from any such animal." (Leviticus 22:25) The rule covers the Israelites and the foreigner alike. Same standard for both.

The answer is True. God says, "You are to keep My commandments and practice them. I am the LORD." (Leviticus 22:31) Keeping them and practicing them go together, bakers. Knowing the recipe is one thing, and baking it is another.

The answer is that He must be acknowledged as holy. God says, "I must be acknowledged as holy among the Israelites." (Leviticus 22:32) Then He adds, "I am the LORD who sanctifies you…" So He asks for it, and He's also the One who makes them holy.

The answer is Egypt! God says He is the One "…who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God." (Leviticus 22:33) He ends the message by reminding them who He is and what He did, friends. Then comes His line again: "I am the LORD."
